correctness.rationale: The non-dominating zero set forces a positive outer vertex with no zero neighbor, hence a positive center and one entirely positive blade. Weight r+1 fails on every other zero blade. At weight r+2, center label one can support at most one additional positive unit beyond the forced blade; m>=3 then leaves a completely zero blade whose zero vertices see total neighboring weight one. Therefore the center has label two and the remaining r units are exactly one label-one on each vertex of the forced blade. The converse satisfies both defining conditions. Exhaustive finite checks agree.

value.rationale: A published theorem determines only the optimum weight on the universal-join family. For generalized windmills with at least three blades, the present result completely resolves the equality case and gives the exact number of optima. This is a natural structural refinement on a standard named graph family and exposes a genuine boundary at two blades.
